Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the supplies and travel share you accept, the days of supplies to hold, the days before a service warning and the repair limit.
Check Supply Items and Stock: the pack, the unit cost, the reorder point and the par level of every item. The stock value, the days of cover and the reorder flag fill in by themselves.
Write every purchase on Purchases and every price on Price History; a supplier price rise shows in the change from last month. Compare other suppliers on Supplier Quotes.
Use the Reorder List to order what is low. A labour hour is one cleaner working for one hour and a crew is the cleaners who work together on a job.
Count the stock on Stock Counts and read the value of the difference. Check each van on Van Stock and write spills and waste on Waste and Spills.
Keep every machine on Equipment with its service date, write each service on Equipment Services and plan the next purchase on Replacement Plan.
Read Jobs, Service Months and Cost per Job by Size to see what each job costs before profit, and Travel Cost by Area to see what the road costs.
Use the 14 calculators when you plan: reorder quantity, days of cover, cost per job, budget, unit price, bulk buy, count difference, replace or repair, dilution, travel cost, van load and price rise.
Read the Supplies and Cost Dashboard and the charts every week: spend, cost per job, stock, deliveries, equipment, travel and waste.
Chemical, safety and insurance rules differ by place: check your own local rules before you use any sample wording.
Get every visit paid and see who pays late before cash runs short

every credit with its reason, the approver and the share of the invoice it takes back, so credits never go unseen

deposits for one-off jobs with the job date, the balance after the job and a warning when a deposit is still due
a statement for every client with an open balance, the days since the last one and a printed page ready to send

Invoices with balance, days overdue and days to pay
One row per invoice with the client, the jobs billed, the amount, the due date and the payment; the balance, the days overdue, the days to pay and whether it was paid on time fill in by themselves.
Payments with the days after the due date
One row per payment received with the invoice, the client, the amount and the method; the days after the due date (negative means early), the timing and the client phone fill in by themselves.
Clients with their terms and open balance
The clients with type, area, frequency, payment terms, pay method and status; the open balance and the number of open invoices of each client fill in by themselves.
Aging buckets at each month end
One row per month end and bucket with the unpaid invoices and the amount, counted by how many days past the due date they were; the share of the open amount of that month fills in by itself.
Reminders sent with the schedule check
One row per reminder with the invoice, the ladder step, the channel, who sent it and the day sent; the due date, the balance and the schedule check fill in by themselves.
Credit notes with the share of the invoice
One row per credit note with the invoice, the client, the reason, the amount and who approved it; the share of the invoice it takes back and the phones fill in by themselves.
Late payers with the late share
The clients who paid late three times or more, from every invoice, with the late invoices and the average days late; the open balance and the late share fill in by themselves.
Payment plans with the remaining balance
One row per payment plan with the client, the start date, the total, the instalments and the amount paid so far; the remaining balance, the instalment and the plan status fill in by themselves.
Deposits for one-off jobs with the balance after the job
One row per deposit for a one-off job with the client, the service, the job price and the day the deposit was paid; the balance after the job and the status fill in by themselves.
Disputed invoices with the days open
One row per invoice a client questioned, with the reason, the day it was opened, the day it was resolved and the outcome; the days open and the dispute status fill in by themselves.
One row per balance you gave up with the invoice, the client, the amount, the day it was decided and the reason; the invoice amount, the share written off and the phones fill in by themselves.
Billing runs with the average invoice
One row per billing month with the invoices issued, the total amount and the day the run was done, from every invoice; the average invoice fills in by itself.
Invoice lines with the price per job
One row per invoice with the service billed, the jobs, the labour hours (one cleaner working for one hour) and the amount; the price per job and the price per labour hour fill in by themselves.
The days a client of each type has to pay and the late fee you add when they do not; the invoice builder and the reminder ladder follow these terms.
Pay methods and their share of invoices
The ways each type of client pays with the number of invoices, from every invoice; the share of each method inside its client type fills in by itself.
Statements sent with the days since the last one
One row per statement sent to a client with an open balance, the month it covers and the amount open; the days since the last statement and the statement check fill in.
Direct debit runs with the failure rate

One row per month of direct debit collection with the clients charged, the amount and the failed collections, from every payment; the failure rate and the successful collections fill in by themselves.
Cash received by week with a running total
One row per week with the payments received and the amount, from every payment (the Payments sheet holds the invoices of the demo); the running total fills in by itself.
Collection calls with the promise check
One row per call to a client about an unpaid invoice with the outcome, the day they promised to pay and whether the promise was kept; the promise check and the phones fill in by themselves.

A risk level for a client who pays late
Type the invoices and the late ones in the last 12 months, the average days late, the open balance and the average invoice; see the points from each part, the score from 0 to 100 and the risk level.
Expected cash in the next four weeks
Type the invoices due in each of the next four weeks, the usual delay in days (0 to 14) and the share that is paid; see the cash you expect each week and what is still to come.

Type the failed direct debits in a month, the fee, the minutes to chase each, the cost of an office hour and the delay in days; see the monthly and yearly cost of failures.
